aluminium.rationale: aluminium: metallic lattice; degradation would be redox corrosion, not hydrolysis. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

ceramic.rationale: ceramic: ionic/covalent refractory lattice; no enzyme substrate. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

glass.rationale: glass: Si-O-Si network; no hydrolysable bond accessible to a secreted enzyme at 37 C. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

iron.rationale: iron: metallic lattice; degradation would be redox corrosion, not hydrolysis. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

lead.rationale: lead: metallic lattice; solubilising it would convert a local deposit into systemic exposure. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

silica.rationale: silica: Si-O-Si network; no hydrolysable bond accessible to a secreted enzyme at 37 C. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

steel.rationale: steel: metallic lattice; degradation would be redox corrosion, not hydrolysis. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

stone.rationale: stone: mineral lattice; no enzyme substrate. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.

titanium.rationale: titanium: passivated metallic lattice; no enzyme substrate. No enzymatic degradation route exists; this fragment belongs to the capsule-modulation arm, not the catalyst arm.
